item.title: Critical funding gap threatens health response in Yemen
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) warned that significantly more resources are required to scale up its response in Yemen amid escalating conflict and rising needs.

item.title: Reform, or lose trust: Governments press the UN to reflect the world as it is
item.description: Can the UN still remain relevant if it still looks and acts like the organization it was when it was formed in 1945? The debate over UN reform at the General Assembly in New York last month produced a striking common refrain from a diverse range of Member States.

item.title: WHO releases first global guidelines on child obesity as cases surge
item.description: Child and adolescent obesity has quadrupled since 1990, rising from two per cent to around eight per cent of youngsters in the five-to-19 age group, according to the UN World Health Organization (WHO).

item.title: Kenya races to trace all contacts after first Ebola death, WHO official says
item.description: Kenya’s first Ebola death has triggered a race to trace everyone the victim came into contact with, as the United Nations and partners provide full support, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) top official in the country has told UN News in her first interview on the case.
